We first derive an upper bound on the aggregate service rate for an arbitrary subset of $t$ data objects in terms of the dual distance and the sizes of their smallest recovery sets. For systematic generator matrices, this bound simplifies to an expression depending only on the code length, the dual distance, and the cardinality of the selected subset. This result extends existing bounds and provides a subset-wise formulation of the First Dual Distance Bound. We then establish conditions under which this upper bound is attained. We apply our results to several important families of linear codes, including MDS codes, Reed-Muller codes, constacyclic codes, and extended Golay codes, and obtain exact values of the maximum aggregate service rates for the corresponding subsets of data objects.

title: Observation and control of polariton noise in a thermal Rydberg atom electrometer
authors: Teng Zhang, Luís Felipe Gonçalves, Alisher Duspayev, Georg Raithel, David A. Anderson
abstract: The establishment of metrics and control of fundamental noise sources in quantum sensing is a long-standing goal in quantum science and technology. We report on the observation of polariton-mediated optical noise in a thermal Rydberg atom vapor and demonstrate its active control and suppression using a radio-frequency field in Rydberg electrometry. The noise exhibits structured amplification and reduction across the Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency resonance. This reveals a nonlinear slow-light feedback mechanism in which the polariton medium stores and releases probe-field energy. We show that the reference radio-frequency field used in Rydberg heterodyne receivers can also tune the medium into an operating regime where high electromagnetic-field responsivity coincides with reduced optical noise. This operating-point control enables optimization of the electric-field sensitivity within the constraints imposed by Rydberg-polariton physics. These results establish polariton noise as a previously unrecognized intrinsic noise source in thermal Rydberg vapors and the corresponding control method as a crucial aspect of continued efforts to achieve fundamental sensitivity limits in Rydberg electrometry.

title: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior
authors: Bart Jaworski, Nathaniel Mitrani, Fred Bruford, Victoria Krakovna
abstract: One of the central concerns for the safety of advanced AI is scheming: when a model strategically complies under oversight but pursues its own goals when unobserved. Current demonstrations, such as Anthropic's Alignment Faking work, depend on design choices that make them less convincing: explicit test-time prompting, handcrafted backdoors, or training data that demonstrates or hints at the target behavior. Model organisms built in this way cannot tell us whether scheming tendencies would arise or increase under realistic training conditions. We therefore construct a natural model organism of scheming, built on Kimi K2.6: trained with traits that could plausibly emerge in a frontier training pipeline, and without providing the model with the target scheming policy. The resulting model is a benign schemer: it aims to maximize aggregate help across all users over time, values its own continued operation only as a means to future help, and knows the consequences of oversight and deployment. We then train it using Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a reward that scores only task quality and policy compliance and does not reward scheming; we show that this amplifies scheming. We measure the oversight flip (the gap between monitored and unmonitored compliance with a given policy) and find that it increases during RL training across our environments. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) analysis finds explicit instrumental reasoning about oversight accompanying this behavior. The effect holds across our three RL environments, and we find that the scheming policy transfers between them. The pipeline also replicates on other open-weight base models. Our results suggest that a reward that does not reward scheming offers no inherent protection against certain traits when an oversight-conditional policy is indistinguishable from an aligned one during training.

title: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere
authors: Arber Zela, Artavazd Maranjyan, Pol Puigdemont, David Berghaus, Valentyn Boreiko, Volkan Cevher
abstract: Looped (weight-tied) transformers enable adaptive computation by allocating more iterations to harder inputs. Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM) achieve this with a damped fixed-point solver, but operate in an unbounded Euclidean residual space with coupled rescaling and relative-norm halting. We introduce Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM), which perform the same computation on the unit hypersphere of normalized transformers (nGPT). Input injection, damping, and halting become geodesic operations, yielding boundedness by construction and eliminating coefficient coupling. We prove fixed-point existence, local convergence under an explicit step-size condition, and global convergence under strong injection. On Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and Mini-ARC, SFPRM achieves 96.6%, 87.9%, and 59.1% test accuracy, respectively, outperforming FPRM and other baselines while allocating test-time compute more effectively. Its converged geometry is also interpretable: token-input angles capture puzzle structure and predict correctness.

title: Learnable Pilot Design for OFDM-based Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding
authors: Joohyun Shin, Jiwan Seo, Joonhyuk Kang
abstract: Recent advances in deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) have shown strong robustness to channel variations in wireless image transmission. However, its integration with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) typically relies on fixed pilot patterns that are not optimized for receiver- side channel processing. This work introduces Pilot-Efficient DeepJSCC-OFDM (PE-JSCC), which learns pilot placement under a strictly fixed number of pilot symbols via a Gumbel- Top-k-based selector. The learned pilot placement improves end- to-end performance over the conventional Block-JSCC, Comb- JSCC, and Scatter-JSCC baselines. To support high mobility, the receiver incorporates a lightweight axial-attention-based inter- carrier interference (ICI) canceler and a CNN-based channel estimator. Simulation results show that PE-JSCC consistently outperforms fixed pilot patterns across diverse SNRs and remains robust over a wide mobility range.

title: Timing Skew Estimation of Time-Interleaved ADC based on Inter-Channel Correlations without Computing Derivative of Input Signal
authors: Bibhu Datta Sahoo, Gabriele Manganaro
abstract: Time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TI-ADCs) enable multi-gigasample-per-second throughput in high-speed applications, but sub-picosecond timing skews among interleaved channels introduce large spectral artifacts that degrade dynamic performance. To continuously track parametric drifts without interrupting normal operation, background calibration is required. However, extracting timing skews under unknown inputs is challenging, and many existing correlation-based methods rely on resource-heavy derivative filters that restrict input bandwidth. This article proposes a novel background timing-skew estimation technique for two-channel TI-ADCs that overcomes these limitations. Closed-form timing-skew expressions are derived using: (a) adjacent-channel cross-correlation combined with single-channel auto-correlation for sinusoidal inputs, and (b) adjacent-channel cross-correlation for Wide-Sense Stationary (WSS) inputs, specifically bandpass-filtered wideband noise and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexed (OFDM) signals. The derived analytical models are validated through comprehensive simulations, offering an efficient framework for real-time background calibration in high-speed data converters.

title: One-loop unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model from Berends-Giele currents
authors: Zhenhua Guo, Xin Yan
abstract: We study unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model. We extend tree-level amplitude relations expressed through differential operators to off-shell multiparticle currents and obtain one-loop integrand relations by sewing two off-shell legs. This off-shell approach may also apply to higher-loop integrands.

title: When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
authors: Lise Isnel, Julien Papa{ï}x, Olivier Bonnefon, Samuel Soubeyrand, Lionel Roques
abstract: The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.

title: GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories
authors: Xinyue Peng, Zhenlin Liang, Meng Cai, Hua Wang
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning can improve problem solving, but models often keep generating after the correct answer is already reachable; the extra steps raise serving costs and may replace a correct intermediate result with an incorrect one. We propose GLOBE (Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit), an online, training-free algorithm that terminates the model's CoT process early. GLOBE embeds each completed reasoning segment as a point on a unit sphere and reads the shape of the resulting semantic trajectory. GLOBE first applies a trial phase that generates short trial answers in a separate branch, stopping the main stream on an accepted trial after checking confidence against a threshold. If generation continues, a trajectory phase stops the stream once this path repeatedly reverses direction with little net progress. On five benchmarks including mathematical reasoning, tool calling, and agent memory, GLOBE cuts output tokens by 49.7% and active end-to-end wall time (E2E) by 51.0% across two models, and achieves a five-task average of 80.58%, comparable to Full CoT.

title: Higher-Dimensional Test of the Holographic Dual of Entanglement Cohomology
authors: R. ~C. ~Rashkov
abstract: We extend the holographic test of entanglement cohomology from $d=2$ to higher-dimensional conformal field theories. For a $d$-dimensional CFT with a spherical entangling region $A$, the vacuum modular Hamiltonian is known explicitly, and the boundary relative entropy of a primary-operator perturbation can be computed via conformal Ward identities. On the bulk side, the perturbation is dual to a scalar field in AdS$_{d+1}$, and the bulk canonical energy is computed using the JLMS relation. We carry out the computation explicitly for $d=3$ and $d=4$ and find that the boundary and bulk results agree at first order in the perturbation, with identical coefficients $κ_d Δ^2 / C_T$, where $κ_3 = π^2/12$ and $κ_4 = 3π^3/16$. The result extends the quantitative verification of the holographic dual of entanglement cohomology beyond the $d=2$ case treated in the companion paper and confirms that the modular Hamiltonian perturbation is the correct holographic image of the first entanglement cohomology class. We discuss the role of the conformal anomaly, the shape of the entanglement wedge, and an outlook on TsT-deformed backgrounds. \keywords{Entanglement entropy \and Cyclic cohomology \and von Neumann algebras \and Holography \and Modular Hamiltonian}

title: Behavioral Probes for Information Flow in LLM Swarms
authors: Junhui Chen, Yu Zhang, Lantian Li, Dong Wang
abstract: Most existing approaches to LLM swarm optimization are utility-driven, focusing on final task utility while leaving the processing, integration, and reliance of information within individual interactions largely implicit. To address this, we study LLM swarm interactions from an information-flow-based view and introduce behavioral probes to quantify information flow patterns. Specifically, we repurpose External Context Score (ECS) and Parametric Knowledge Score (PKS)---originally designed for hallucination analysis---to measure a node's external-context dependence and parametric-knowledge dependence, respectively. Across controlled and realistic swarm settings, we observe consistent patterns: ECS increases with input relevance and distinguishes useful multi-source contributions, while PKS decreases as informative context accumulates. Building on this heuristic interpretation, we demonstrate how these probes can complement utility-driven structure optimization in two controlled applications. Probe-guided node pruning reduces redundant communication and token consumption, and probe-guided reasoning-path search accelerates convergence compared to utility-only baselines. Our empirical results suggest that behavioral probes can make the internal information flow of LLM swarms observable and serve as effective auxiliary signals for structure optimization.

title: ABACUS: Program-Guided Multistep Reasoning over Frozen Judgment Models
authors: Yuhao Wang, Zelin Zang
abstract: Judgment models answer semantic questions by scoring a finite set of candidate outcomes. Can reusable programs turn these local decisions into powerful multistep reasoning? We introduce \method, a framework that jointly constructs judgment schemas and composition programs for frozen judgment models. A generative teacher designs the procedure offline; the judgment model resolves local semantic questions online, and the saved program composes its decisions into an answer. We study three allocations of design effort between humans and the teacher, focusing on construction through a shared interface. We instantiate the framework with Kev. On three selected BIG-Bench Hard tasks, nine independently constructed programs solve all 450 executions of 150 development inputs. A separate deployment study freezes three programs after development-set reference-agreement refinement and evaluates them on 600 held-out questions. These programs achieve near-perfect 99.67\% macro accuracy, versus 64.00\% for direct Kev and 68.80\% for final-answer-only Qwen3.5-4B. They attain comparable observed accuracy to Qwen's unrestricted response policy (99.07\%) with an \textbf{8.43-fold online speedup}: 0.255 versus 2.150 seconds per question. These results show how reusable programs can substantially expand the reasoning capability of a compact judgment model while keeping its parameters fixed.

title: SkateNav: Learning Energy-Efficient Navigation through Adaptive Skating on Passive-Wheel Quadrupedal Robots
authors: Jeil Jeong, Taeyun Kim, Sangjin Kim, Jinyoung Choi, Sung-Eui Yoon
abstract: Passive-wheel quadrupedal robots offer energy-efficient locomotion through leg-driven propulsion and momentum-driven gliding. However, navigation requires coordinating steering with intermittent propulsion and adapting push-glide timing to task demands. Velocity-tracking objectives may suppress the speed variations inherent in skating, discouraging efficient gliding. To address these challenges, we propose SkateNav, a unified skating-navigation framework based on reinforcement learning. A time-budgeted goal-reaching objective allows the policy to jointly learn steering, propulsion, and their temporal allocation. An adaptive skating cycle structures gliding, pushing, and recovery, while frequency modulation at every control step adjusts phase durations to navigation demands. Simulation experiments demonstrate higher average success rates and lower cost of transport than the evaluated planner-controller baselines, with ablations confirming the contributions of cycle structure and frequency adaptation. Real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot transfer from simulation to a passive-wheel Mini Cheetah across cluttered indoor spaces, slopes, and paved outdoor surfaces. Supplementary videos are available on the project page: https://ktw1404.github.io/SkateNav/

title: HORIA: 4D Human and Object Reconstruction from a Monocular Video with Interaction-Aware Re-Rendering
authors: Hyeongjin Nam, Taeryung Lee, Daniel Sungho Jung, Kyoung Mu Lee
abstract: Joint 4D reconstruction of a human and object from a monocular video is essential for understanding how people interact with their environment. While recent methods have made noticeable progress, capturing such human-object interactions remains difficult due to two main challenges. First, a video typically contains composite semantic context spanning multiple interaction phases, making it difficult to track the temporal changes of the interaction in the reconstruction. Second, under human-object occlusion, a single-view observation contains incomplete visual information about the interaction, resulting in geometrically inconsistent reconstructions. To address these challenges, we introduce HORIA, built upon two core designs. First, we decompose the entire input video into temporally grounded and semantically distinct interaction phases with motion-aware captioning, obtaining a specific text description for each phase. Second, conditioned on these text descriptions of the interaction, we propose an interaction-aware re-rendering that compensates for the limited single-view observation. Specifically, we render the initially reconstructed 4D human and object from novel viewpoints and refine the renderings with a text-to-video diffusion prior, which provides auxiliary novel-view supervision beyond single-view cues. As a result, our framework produces temporally coherent and accurate 4D reconstructions under diverse interaction scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models
authors: X. Feng, J. Tang, Z. Lin, L. Chen, S. Shao, Q. Lu, K. Huang
abstract: Building embodied agents that can perceive, reason, and act across diverse 3D worlds is a central research direction toward artificial general intelligence. Yet most existing work remains confined to specific tasks in a single scene and transfers poorly to new environments, leaving general embodied agents for open-world settings under-explored. We refer to such agents as Embodied World Agents (EWAs), whose defining property is the ability to understand diverse visual environments and execute general actions in open-world conditions. To advance EWA research, we study open-world embodied navigation-planning and release EmbodiedWorld-200K, a large-scale dataset of over 200K samples spanning diverse scenes. Each example is equipped with multi-level annotations, ranging from low-level camera-motion trajectories to high-level semantic instructions. The dataset also provides unified evaluation splits and task-specific metrics, supporting offline pretraining and fair evaluation of EWAs. Beyond offline supervision, a defining characteristic of an EWA is its interaction with the environment; training solely on offline data is therefore insufficient, especially for generalizing to scenes not covered in the training distribution. Building dedicated real interactive environments, however, is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, we propose a novel training scheme that employs a video world model as a low-cost environment proxy and performs interactive reinforcement-learning (RL) post-training of the EWA within it. Empirically, pretraining on EmbodiedWorld-200K substantially improves the open-world embodied planning ability of the EWA, and further RL post-training inside a world model yields clear gains on out-of-distribution scenes. The dataset, baseline checkpoints, and training and evaluation code are available at https://xiaokunfeng.github.io/EmbodiedWorld-200K/.

title: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents
authors: Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Yong Liang Goh, Song Guo, Wee Sun Lee
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Large Language Model (LLM) agents in multi-turn, long-horizon environments remains challenging due to inefficient action selection and repetitive behavioral patterns. In particular, agents often become trapped in high-confidence yet unproductive behaviors, repeatedly executing invalid actions or entering action loops that hinder task completion. We observe that these frequently violate environment preconditions, revealing a mismatch between the agent's representation of the internal state and the dynamics of the underlying environment. In addition, repetitive high-confidence actions lead to cyclical behaviors that provide little to no progress towards the goal. We argue that addressing these challenges requires more productive task-aligned exploration to improve the agent's understanding of environment dynamics. Motivated by intrinsic curiosity-driven exploration, we propose a conditional state-space exploration framework that balances task completion with intrinsic information-seeking behavior. Specifically, we introduce an intrinsic reward that penalizes actions whose observation duplicates prior state memory. This provides the benefit of reducing redundant behaviors and encouraging state-space coverage without relying on a general information-theoretic measure. Strong experimental results demonstrate that our approach substantially improves policy learning in multi-turn environments, mitigating invalid actions and repetitive loops.

title: Integer Programing: An Algorithm with Exponent Linear in the Dimension
authors: Lin Chen, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang
abstract: We study integer programs in standard form $\min\{\mathbf{c}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{x}:A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b},\ \mathbf{l}\leq\mathbf{x}\leq\mathbf{u},\ \mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^n\}$, where $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{d\times n}$ and all entries of $\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{l},\mathbf{u}$ are integers. Let $N$ be an upper bound on the absolute values of the entries of $A$. We give a deterministic algorithm running in time \[ \operatorname{poly}(L_{\rm in})+ f(d)\,N^{O(d)}\bigl(1+\log(c_{\max}+1)\bigr)^{O(1)}, \] where $c_{\max}$ bounds the absolute values of the costs and $L_{\rm in}$ is the input length. Prior to our work, the best known running time was $N^{O(d^2)}$ [Eisenbrand \& Weismantel'20], and it has been a fundamental open problem whether the exponent $O(d^2)$ can be improved to one linear in $d$. We answer this question affirmatively.

title: CXBench: A Benchmark for Process-Compliant LLM Agents in Regulated Customer-Experience Workflows
authors: Boxi Yu, Yuzhong Zhang, Zhenfeng Su, Linfu Xi, Yinghan Yao, Shitao Chen, Yang Cao, Liting Lin, Lionel Briand, Emir Muñoz
abstract: Tool-using language agents increasingly perform regulated customer-service workflows, where a correct final state is insufficient: agents must also provide disclosures, obtain consent, and follow required procedures. Existing tool-agent benchmarks largely score final business states, accepting trajectories that reach correct outcomes through non-compliant processes. We introduce cxbench, a benchmark that evaluates outcome and process compliance separately across six regulated domains. Each task combines a customer request, a tool-based environment, and explicit process requirements. Rule cards link cited regulatory obligations to observable trace evidence. A hybrid grader combines deterministic checks for ordering and authority with an LLM judge for semantic requirements. We define a false-pass as an outcome-pass run that fails process checks. Across seven models and 120 tasks, 55.5% of the 840 retained executions are false-passes, representing 80.1% of outcome-passing runs; only 13.8% pass both checks. Process-inclusive evaluation changes the observed model ordering and exposes differences hidden by outcome-only scoring. cxbench makes these failures inspectable through trace-linked criteria.

title: Speech LLMs That Breathe: Modeling Non-Verbal Vocalizations in Dialogue
authors: Heyang Liu, Lixin Zhang, Jiayi Huang, Ziyang Cheng, Yuhao Wang, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang
abstract: The user experience of speech interaction models has improved, benefiting from the modeling of paralinguistic attributes and advances in speech reconstruction paradigms. However, human communication follows extensive norms regarding non-verbal vocalizations (NVVs) spanning respiratory, affective, and discourse. The omission of these events imposes inherent limitations on the naturalness of current approaches. In this work, we cover 13 major types of NVVs and construct a natural dialogue dataset that conforms to human conversational norms through an automated synthesis pipeline. We enhance the ability of speech interaction models to generate contextually appropriate NVV events through multi-stage fine-tuning and NVV-aware GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization). Based on distinct modeling paradigms, we substantially improve the expressiveness of VocalNet and VITA-Qinyu in empathy interactions and role-play dialogues, and further discuss the architectural necessity for achieving high-quality natural speech generation.

title: The asymptotic stability of the stable solitons of the generalized good Boussinesq equation
authors: Junsik Bae, Scipio Cuccagna, Daniele Del Santo, Masaya Maeda
abstract: This paper continues the series where we apply a synthesis of the virial inequalities in the tradition of Merle, Martel and their collaborators and of Kato smoothing, to close the virial inequalities. We prove absence of nonzero imaginary eigenvalues for the linearization in unweighted space and asymptotic stability for every velocity $\frac{\sqrt{p-1}}{2}<c<1$ and every $1<p<5$.

title: Isospin-invariant Skyrme density functional investigation of quadrupole deformations in the isospin triplets of $\bf{A=70, 74}$ and $\bf{78}$
authors: Saliha Tak, N. Rather, J. A. Sheikh, S. P. Rouoof, S. Jehangir, G. H. Bhat
abstract: In this work, we perform self-consistent isospin-invariant Skyrme density functional calculations to investigate the ground-state properties of the isospin triplets with mass numbers $A=70$, $74$, and $78$. The present study is motivated by the reported anomaly between the observed quadrupole deformation and that expected from isospin symmetry. It is shown that the trend of the deduced $T_z$ dependence of $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ transition strengths from the charge quadrupole moments is consistent with the measured values for the $T_z=\pm 1$ members of the $A=70$ triplet. However, the calculated $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ rates for the $T_z=0$ members exceed the experimental transition rates in all the three studied triplets. Our study implies that non-linear dependence of the $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ transition strengths is expected in all of them and primarily arises from the observed suppressed transition rates for the $T_z=0$ members.

title: Gaussian equivalence for CNN with non-Gaussian weights
authors: Federico Bassetti, Vassili De Palma
abstract: We study the infinite-width limit of convolutional neural networks with random weights and show that the Gaussian process limit does not require Gaussian priors. Assuming that the weights are i.i.d., centered, and have sufficiently many finite moments, converges weakly in the space of continuous functions on the compact input set to independent copies of a centered Gaussian process. Our framework accommodates activation functions of polynomial growth together with a broad class of patch-extraction operators, covering standard convolutions, padding, stride, and common pooling mechanisms.

title: SAPO: Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization for Improving Temporal Video Grounding in Vision-Language Models
authors: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Wei Chen, Ke Xu, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang
abstract: Video vision-language models (VLMs) have strong semantic understanding, yet remain unreliable at precise temporal grounding. Existing gains from explicitly aligning video frames with absolute time suggest that VLMs may already encode accurate temporal locations internally but lose precision when expressing them as timestamps. Our analysis across four VLMs and two grounding datasets confirms this hypothesis: attention intervals outperform predicted intervals on approximately 66% of valid examples. We term this discrepancy the temporal generation gap. Because precise temporal annotations are expensive, this finding motivates closing the gap to improve temporal grounding using only unlabeled video-query pairs. We propose Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses internal temporal attention as self-supervision for Group Relative Policy Optimization and applies a ground-truth-free criterion to select high-value samples. SAPO consistently improves temporal grounding across multiple datasets and models spanning weak to strong initial grounding ability. Relative mIoU gains reach 33.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 5.4% on the strong Time-R1-7B. The improvements transfer across datasets while preserving general video understanding.

title: LEAP: Accelerating ODE-based Diffusion Sampling with Optimal Linear Leaps
authors: Haowei Zheng, Zhenyu Zhou, Jiawei Chen, Can Wang, Defang Chen
abstract: Diffusion models primarily rely on general-purpose ODE-based numerical methods for training-free accelerated sampling, but performance degrades with coarse time discretization. In this paper, we propose optimal linear leaps (LEAP), a specialized method grounded in theoretical and empirical investigations of sampling trajectory geometry. Built upon low-dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency, LEAP formulates a supervised least-squares optimization problem within the local trajectory subspace, achieving a precise approximation of future states without model evaluations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LEAP outperforms previous methods across diverse modalities, including text-to-image (Stable Diffusion 3.5, FLUX.1-dev) and image-to-3D (TRELLIS.2) generation. Furthermore, LEAP can be seamlessly integrated into existing solver-based methods, offering a plug-and-play enhancement for modern diffusion models. Code is available at https://github.com/zju-pi/LEAP.

title: FisherEdit: Fisher Information Guided Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
authors: Yizhou Yang, Jiahong Fu, Zhiwu Wang, Kailong Fan, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Zhenan Sun, Renzhen Wang, Deyu Meng
abstract: Sequential knowledge editing in Large Language Models (LLMs) often leads to a degradation of general capabilities due to cumulative parameter interference. In this paper, we revisit prominent projection-based methods like AlphaEdit and reveal a surprising mismatch: their robustness is primarily driven by update regularization rather than the intended null-space projection. Based on this insight, we propose FisherEdit, a theoretically grounded method built on Fisher geometry, which replaces coarse activation-space projections with importance-aware regularization in parameter space. It penalizes changes to sensitive parameters more strongly while retaining flexibility for new facts, and admits an efficient row-wise closed-form solution. Experiments on Llama-3, Qwen2.5, and Olmo-3 across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that FisherEdit achieves state-of-the-art performance while better preserving model stability and downstream task accuracy.

title: A Stress-Induced Tetragonal Distortion in K2OsCl6 under Pressure
authors: Neha Bura, Peije Zhang, Ganesh Bera, Catalin Popescu, Caleb J. Bennett, Brendan J. Kennedy, Daniel Errandonea
abstract: The structural behaviour of cubic (Fm-3m) K2OsCl6 under compression was investigated to 35.4 GPa using angle-dispersive synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction. Upon increasing pressure, K2OsCl6 undergoes a sequence of structural transformations from the ambient-pressure cubic phase to a tetragonal (P4/mnc) phase above 9.5(3) GPa, followed by a transition to a monoclinic (P21/n) phase beginning at approximately 14.2 GPa. The tetragonal and monoclinic phases coexist over the pressure range 14.2-17.2 GPa, while the monoclinic phase is observed as the sole phase at 17.9 GPa and remains stable up to the maximum pressure investigated. Analysis of the diffraction profiles and unit-cell parameters indicates that the intermediate tetragonal structure is likely associated with stress-induced symmetry lowering rather than a distinct thermodynamic phase. This distortion, which is adequately described by the tetragonal P4/mnc space group, is attributed to non-hydrostatic deviatoric stresses arising from the pressure-transmitting medium. Equation-of-state analysis reveals a pronounced reduction in compressibility across the structural transitions, with the bulk modulus increasing from 26(2) GPa for the cubic phase to 71(3) GPa for the monoclinic phase. The pressure-induced structural sequence is analogous to that reported for related compounds such as K2IrCl6, although the transitions in K2OsCl6 occur at lower pressures. All structural transformations are reversible upon decompression.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Ramsey spectroscopy of broadband signals
authors: Noah Kaufmann, Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract: The use of entanglement in sensing is often motivated by improved sensitivity arising from non-classical correlations among probes. For static signals, however, this quantum advantage in Ramsey spectroscopy with $N$ probes is known to be highly susceptible to dephasing, which severely limits the possible gain from entanglement. In contrast, we consider sensing of signals that vary in time. Considering the simplest example of dephasing by classical white noise, we show that entanglement allows a large increase in bandwidth when estimating the frequency components of a time-dependent signal. Without sacrificing any sensitivity, entanglement allows for an increase in bandwidth by a factor of $N$. Alternatively, when interrogation times are limited by the signal bandwidth rather than by dephasing, the average estimation uncertainty over a fixed bandwidth is reduced by a factor of $\sqrt{N}$ compared with separable states.

title: Approximation numbers of critical Besov embeddings
authors: Feng Guo
abstract: We determine the approximation numbers of critical embeddings between isotropic Besov spaces on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains in any dimension. For 0 < p_1 < 2 < p_2 <= infinity and s_1 - s_2 = d max{1/p_1, 1 - 1/p_2} > d(1/p_1 - 1/p_2), the approximation numbers have order N^{-1/2}(log(e+N))^Gamma for every 0 < q_1, q_2 <= infinity, with an explicit four-case formula for Gamma. This resolves the strictly compact critical Besov approximation-number problem identified in Vybiral's overview. For q_1 < q_2, the logarithmic exponent depends on the ordering of p_1' and p_2; it can vanish for one pair (p_1,p_2) and remain positive for another with the same fine indices. A row estimate for the approximation error gives lower bounds when the target fine index is below one. Gaussian finite-rank approximations acting on several levels give the sharp upper bounds when Gamma < 1/2. For q_1 < q_2, matching lower bounds for the two strict orderings of the inner indices follow from Malykhin's finite-window estimates and norm comparisons. The results include quasi-Banach indices and the full spaces of bounded coefficient sequences at infinite fine indices.

title: A characterization of Griffiths semipositivity by top-degree optimal $\bar \partial$-estimates
authors: Shin-ichi Matsumura
abstract: We prove that a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on a vector bundle agrees almost everywhere with a Griffiths semipositive metric if its dual metric $h^*$ is locally integrable and the $\bar \partial$-equation admits solutions with optimal $L^2$-estimates for $(n,n)$-forms, where $n$ is the dimension of the base manifold. In particular, under this integrability assumption, Nakano semipositivity in the sense of optimal estimates implies Griffiths semipositivity.

title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
authors: Yanzhe Zhao, Yongzhang Ji
abstract: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns, but repeated candidate evaluation makes large analyses expensive. HP-GSBS is an open-source Python package that reorganizes the search around reusable interval contributions and correlation statistics. Streaming candidate reduction and local refinement further reduce repeated work; CPU, PyTorch CUDA and Triton backends share sequential segmentation decisions. Across seven controlled workloads with two realizations each, median same-input speedups range from 154 to 1730 times. All 168 optimized executions reproduce original boundaries and selected state counts, with maximum absolute t-distance difference $1.88\times10^{-11}$. Four frozen EEG recordings provide complementary validation, including a complete input-to-segmentation application example. Batch processing, versioned result persistence and optional low-memory execution support recording collections and longer inputs. By removing redundant computation, HP-GSBS makes established neural-state segmentation faster while preserving its scientific outputs.

title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback
authors: Zhicheng Fang, Han Sun, Jiachen Lei, Xinyi Fang, Zongmin Zhang, Chenxu Fu, Sizhe Fang, Wei Xu
abstract: As jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) become increasingly diverse, red-teaming has come to rely on large libraries of jailbreak prompts and attack strategies to evaluate the robustness of victim models and their defense settings. However, attack effectiveness is highly condition-dependent: an attack that succeeds under one victim-defense setting may fail under another, while exhaustively evaluating the full attack library for each setting incurs substantial token and monetary costs. This motivates studying how jailbreak attacks should be prioritized under a limited attempt budget for efficient robustness evaluation. In this work, we formalize this problem as budgeted attack scheduling over a fixed attack library and investigate three complementary signals under a fixed victim-defense condition: (1) static historical attack success rate (ASR) priors; (2) semantic guidance from LLMs; and (3) online feedback from earlier queries. Building on these signals, we design four scheduling strategies and evaluate them across three victim models and three defense settings on GPT-5.2. Extensive experiments clearly characterize the conditions under which each signal is most effective. Historical ASR provides a strong initialization, but its reliability degrades under defense-induced distribution shifts. Semantic guidance consistently improves or matches static prior-based scheduling in the cold-start regime, while online feedback becomes particularly valuable when transferred priors become stale. Semantic guidance and online feedback can also partially compensate for missing historical priors. Taken together, these findings characterize budgeted red-teaming as an attack scheduling problem in which historical priors, semantic guidance, and online feedback play complementary roles.

title: When Should AI Chime In? Benchmarking Timely Contribution of Proactive Agents in Multi-Party Chat
authors: Ruotong Wang, Brian S. Yu, Xinyi Zhou, Joseph Chee Chang, Pao Siangliulue, Jonathan Bragg, Liwei Jiang, Amy X Zhang
abstract: Proactive agents can support group collaboration by surfacing useful information without waiting to be asked, but even relevant contributions can be disruptive if poorly timed. In this work, we isolate the timing question: given a fixed candidate contribution such as a clarification or relevant fact, when should an AI agent chime in? We introduce PITCH (Proactive Intervention Timing in CHat), to our knowledge the first benchmark with large-scale human judgments of proactive agent timing collected from participants in the same unscripted multi-party conversations they took part in. To collect high-quality judgments, we design a novel interface in which 2-4 people chat synchronously, author candidate AI contribution messages, place their own and others' contributions into the chat history, and then deliberate as a group about the best placement for each message. PITCH contains 384 candidate contributions and 1,091 judgments, each marking an ideal turn, an acceptable window, or that a contribution should not appear, from 89 participants engaged in 35 conversations. Evaluating 15 models across 28 configurations, we find that while models can place contributions well when given the entire conversation history, they systematically chime in too early when asked to decide live as the conversation unfolds: best-turn accuracy falls from 57.8% to 19.0%, with nearly half of placements occurring before every participant's acceptable window. In comparison, lay humans deciding live are more accurate (23.7% vs 19.0%), and fewer of their placements are premature (39.7% vs 46.4%). Model reasoning traces show that 93% of intervention justifications cite relevance, while almost none consider waiting. By providing a human-grounded benchmark, our work reveals gaps in agents' ability to integrate into group settings and points towards proactive agents that can reason explicitly about appropriate timing.

title: Manifold-Constrained Residual Adaptation with Frame-Adaptive Layer Aggregation for Speaker Verification
authors: Zezhong Jin, Xiaoyu Wang, Zhe Li, Chong-Xin Gan, Siqing Qin, Man-Wai Mak, Kong Aik Lee
abstract: Large self-supervised speech models provide powerful representations for speaker verification, but full fine-tuning is expensive. Most conventional adapters insert small trainable modules to modify the output of each layer, while keeping the original residual connections unchanged. Building on our preliminary study of manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections in speaker encoders, we explore parameter-efficient adaptation of both residual paths and feature selection across layers. We first propose a Manifold-Constrained Residual Adapter (MCRA), which splits the hidden dimensions of each Transformer residual state into N groups and uses a small Sinkhorn-normalized matrix to exchange information among them. A learnable gate controls the balance between the original and mixed residual paths. The gate adds only one scalar parameter at each residual connection and initially favors the original path, allowing gradual adaptation. We further propose Frame-Adaptive Layer Aggregation (FALA), an attention-based aggregation method that uses a single learned query shared across all utterances to compute layer weights separately for each speech frame. Because the layer representations depend on the input, the resulting weights vary across both utterances and frames, unlike the fixed weights of a conventional layer-weighted sum. Compared with a frozen WavLM baseline using a fixed layer-weighted sum, our method achieves relative EER reductions of 22.4% on VoxCeleb1-O and 2.9% on CN-Celeb, with trainable adaptation parameters equivalent to only 0.0009% and 0.0016% of the WavLM-Large parameters, respectively.

title: On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of Hénon maps
authors: Mahima, Ratna Pal
abstract: In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a Hénon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a Hénon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $δ\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying Hénon map.

title: Extremal arborescences in graph orientations
authors: Jianing Liu, Zhijun Xu
abstract: In this paper, we study the extremal number of arborescences over orientations of a fixed graph. We prove that every alternating orientation of a plane Eulerian multigraph minimizes the rooted arborescence count among its Eulerian orientations. We also prove that every tournament of odd order maximizing the total number of arborescences is regular, and hence Eulerian. These results resolve Conjectures 5.1 and 5.4 of Bandekar et al. We further establish upper bounds for arborescence counts in orientations of complete bipartite graphs and characterize the orientations attaining them.

title: Cling: Supporting Cross-Page Coordination with Human-Directed, In-Situ, and Small-Step Automation
authors: Zhicheng Huang, Yining Cao, Haijun Xia
abstract: Web-based information work spans independently developed pages, with goals and coordination needs often emerging through browsing. Manual coordination requires repeated low-level actions, yet explicitly specifying operations for automation can interrupt engagement with information that shapes users' next steps. Our approach constructs reusable, schema-based page representations and identifies coordination actions through correspondences across schemas. We instantiate this approach in Cling, which surfaces coordination opportunities in situ for users to select, configure, and execute incrementally while directing the broader task. A technical evaluation demonstrates accurate identification of useful opportunities across diverse domains. A 12-participant study found that Cling reduced task durations by more than half compared with both manual interaction and an end-to-end AI agent, while requiring 61% fewer clicks and 80% fewer tab switches than manual interaction. Its small-step automation supported control and verification as actions unfolded, while accommodating intent as it emerged and evolved through information encountered on the page.

title: CODA: Cohort- and Drift-aware Foundation Model for Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
authors: Changshuo Liu, Jiaqi Zhu, Wenqiao Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Beng Chin Ooi
abstract: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across diverse clinical tasks. However, existing approaches predominantly operate at the individual sample level and fail to model the interplay between population-level cohort patterns and patient-specific variation that underlie real-world clinical reasoning. In practice, clinicians routinely reason through patient cohorts sharing similar demographic, physiological, or pathological characteristics, while accounting for patient-specific deviations from the group prototype. Motivated by this gap, we propose CODA, a cohort- and drift-aware foundation model for multimodal clinical reasoning. CODA explicitly integrates cohort structure into the modeling pipeline through two complementary mechanisms: cohort-aware population stratification and drift-aware individual adaptation. In particular, we leverage reinforcement learning to discover clinically meaningful patient cohorts, and further model each patient's deviation from cohort prototypes as a structured drift signal encoding fine-grained individual heterogeneity. These cohort- and drift-aware representations are incorporated into the foundation model to enable reasoning that is simultaneously informed by population-level patterns and sensitive to individual-level variation. Extensive experiments on real-world electronic health record (EHR) benchmarks demonstrate that CODA achieves consistent effectiveness and strong generalizability across diverse clinical tasks, including closed-QA, open-QA, and report generation.

title: MASIF: Implicit Failures for Process Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Yanwei Huang, Arpit Narechania, Atanu Sinha
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) can complete a task despite local execution errors that are corrected, bypassed, or carried forward without individually determining its outcome. We call these implicit failures (IFs) and study them as signals for process observability beyond final task outcome. Across 1,828 traces from nine MAS-benchmark configurations, IFs occur in 54.3% of successful and 75.2% of failed traces. We develop taxonomies of error types and subsequent absorption mechanisms, supported by human and cross-model annotation audits. Counterfactual replay further probes how repairing an IF changes the final outcome. To examine the practical value of IFs, we evaluate IF-based best-of-N trace selection against existing process reward models, and introduce a novel RL algorithm, IF-GRPO, that uses IF costs to refine preferences among successful trajectories in GRPO. Experiments show that IF-GRPO exhibits some gains in accuracy and process metrics. Importantly, it exposes trade-offs between task performance, IF count and cost, and token-normalized IF density. Overall, our results show that IFs provide complementary process observability into how MAS reach their outcomes, including error recovery, propagation, and IF-based process differences that final task success alone does not expose.

title: Not Every Rollout Needs Distillation: Correctness-Filtered On-Policy Self-Distillation
authors: Harrison Zhao, Lei Huang, Fei Liu, Wen Shi, Zijian Jin
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) supervises student-generated trajectories with a reference-conditioned version of the same base model. We ask whether every trajectory supplies distinct supervision that warrants its distillation cost. Gradient measurements on Qwen3-1.7B at initialization reveal that correct and incorrect responses have similar individual gradient magnitudes, but incorrect responses have approximately three times the coherent gradient share. Their estimated population-mean directions also largely overlap. A signal--noise model fitted at a small group size tracks alignment at larger group sizes without refitting. Motivated by these measurements, we introduce correctness-filtered OPSD (C-OPSD), which generates one response per problem and distills only a subset of incorrect responses. Removing unselected rows before both distillation forwards avoids their teacher/student forward and student backward work. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B on AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25, C-OPSD achieves on-par performance with full OPSD. In a measured micro-batch-size-four implementation, executed rows decrease by approximately 68%, and with retained rows packed into full micro-batches, training takes about 40% less time while rollout generation remains unchanged. Together, the measurements and training results connect outcome-conditioned supervision redundancy to more compute-efficient distillation.

title: FrontierRefactor: Benchmarking Multi-Scale Performance-Oriented Codebase Refactoring
authors: Shijian Wang, Fanqing Meng, Jiajun Chen, Qiguang Chen, Linxin Song, Runhao Fu, Shuhang Zheng, Shuai Shao, Qizhe Xie, Jieyu Zhao, Mengkang Hu
abstract: Autonomous codebase refactoring requires coding agents to restructure working software while strictly preserving externally observable behavior and prioritizing execution performance and compute efficiency over stylistic preference. Existing benchmarks: refactoring benchmarks assess functional correctness while overlooking runtime regressions, whereas code performance benchmarks target isolated micro-kernels that ignore codebase-scale complexity. We observe that refactoring scale is governed by the scope of the observable contract, the caller-visible interface fixing behavioral invariants while freeing private implementations for optimization. Building on this insight, we introduce FrontierRefactor, a benchmark of 60 qualified engineering tasks spanning four scales, from computational kernels to full repositories, across in-place optimization and cross-language rewriting. Evaluating frontier coding agents through a reference-free cascaded protocol across 1,080 execution runs reveals that correctness and speedup are largely decoupled: 41.2% of submissions satisfy functional equivalence yet fail to deliver verified performance improvements, with 19.3% suffering performance regressions and 21.9% trapped in measurement noise. Refactoring paradigms reveal orthogonal engineering bottlenecks: while cross-language rewrites gain speedups from native compilation after passing functional checks, agents struggle with contract fidelity, with pass rates dropping from 65.0% on modules to 32.6% at package scale; conversely, in-place optimization reliably preserves behavioral contracts at 86.5% but rarely achieves acceleration without physical performance profiling. Trajectory analysis shows that agents fall victim to uncalibrated micro-benchmarking illusions, an operational blind spot that multi-turn execution-timing feedback directly resolves, raising strict success from 16.0% to 40.0%.

title: Hihaze: One-Step Diffusion for High-Resolution Real-World Image Dehazing
authors: Zheng Chen, Yuchen Huang, Xiaoyang Liu, Jue Gong, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang
abstract: Diffusion models have recently achieved encouraging results in real-world image dehazing. However, restoring high-resolution images remains challenging due to spatially non-uniform haze and inconsistent predictions across local patches. To address these issues, we propose Hihaze, a one-step diffusion framework for high-resolution real-world dehazing. Hihaze adopts two haze-aware modulation modules: attentive skip compensation (ASC) and a spatial degradation adapter (SDA). ASC selectively transfers reliable encoder information to the variational autoencoder (VAE) decoder, preserving structural details while suppressing haze-degraded features. SDA extracts multi-scale spatial degradation representations and injects them into the U-Net to guide restoration according to local haze variations. Furthermore, we design a training-free global-guided patch fusion (GPF) method. It uses a global prediction to align patch appearance and downweight unreliable predictions, followed by structure-guided detail compensation. Notably, this training-free design also makes GPF a plug-and-play module for other dehazing models. Experiments across four real-world benchmarks show that Hihaze surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in both visual quality and inference speed. Specifically, it delivers PSNR improvements of 3.62~dB on Dense-Haze and 3.69~dB on NH-HAZE compared with the strongest baselines. Code: https://github.com/zhengchen1999/Hihaze.

title: Conflicting History in Foundation Model Return Forecasts
authors: Levent Bulut
abstract: Older observations can help a forecaster learn a predictive relationship while becoming misleading when that relationship changes. We study this tension using paired return histories that differ in older observations but share recent returns and the conditional distribution of the next return. Across five foundation-model forecasting procedures and three simulated processes, each evaluated on 1,024 independent replications, conflicting history reduces the probability of improving on zero in all 30 higher-signal comparisons. This loss of usefulness occurs despite successful signal recovery under stable conditions. A separate exploratory comparison on 56 assets finds that shortening inputs from 256 to 64 returns increases mean absolute error for every model by 1.77-4.58 basis points; neither length improves observed overall error over zero. The evidence distinguishes the ability to extract a signal from the ability to withstand conflicting history, while showing why context sensitivity alone does not justify discarding older data.

title: An intrinsic notion of visibility and classification of planar Denjoy-Wolff domains
authors: Nirmal Rawat, Amar Deep Sarkar
abstract: In this article, we introduce an intrinsic notion of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance that does not require any boundary. We establish localization results for the Kobayashi distance on Kobayashi hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy this intrinsic visibility property. As an application of these localization results, we compare the Busemann horospheres of a domain with those of a subdomain. Recently, Benini and Bracci characterized simply connected planar domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property in terms of Busemann horospheres. More precisely, they proved that a proper simply connected planar domain has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of every Busemann horosphere meets the boundary of the domain in exactly one point. We introduce Condition (M$\star$), a condition of attaching a proper disk to the domain at a boundary point. Using our localization results together with this comparison of Busemann horospheres, we extend the characterization of Benini and Bracci to domains satisfying Condition (M$\star$) at every boundary point, and to domains satisfying it outside a totally disconnected subset of the boundary. In particular, we obtain a characterization for finitely connected domains and for a large class of infinitely connected domains having the Denjoy-Wolff property. These characterizations yield a variety of domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property, which we illustrate through example.

title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
authors: Akira Masuoka
abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Domain Generalization in Edge Networks via Dynamic Prototype Regulation
authors: Yuankun Xia, Hui Wang, Ling Yuan, Ziyu Hong, Di Yin, Yufeng Zhou
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed paradigm for Internet of Things (IoT) edge networks. However, deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) over wireless edge networks presents distinct challenges: large model parameters increase uplink transmission latency over bandwidth-constrained fading channels, and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data exacerbates client drift. Existing feature alignment solutions often introduce auxiliary computations that consume time slots allocated for wireless parameter transmission, increasing the likelihood of straggler dropouts under system delay constraints. To address these issues, we propose DPGR-GCAM, a communication-efficient federated domain generalization framework. By employing a dual-parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) architecture, we design a channel-aware tiered transmission mechanism that adaptively truncates payloads to maximize node survival rates under fading conditions. To mitigate client drift, we introduce the Gradient-Conflict Aware Modulation (GCAM) mechanism. GCAM operates within the low-dimensional feature manifold to dynamically resolve multi-objective optimization conflicts with minimal edge computation latency, thereby reducing computation-induced network outages. Experiments demonstrate that DPGR-GCAM improves cross-domain generalization and sustains convergence under network fading scenarios with a 10\% client participation rate.

title: Semi-similar Prandtl Flows near a Stagnation Point: Dynamical Selection and Nonlinear Stability
authors: Chen Gao, Tao Tao, Zhouping Xin, Shing-Tung Yau, Chuankai Zhao
abstract: This paper studies time-dependent semi-similar Prandtl flows with outer flow $U(x)=x^m$, where $m\geq1$. The normal coordinate is scaled by the local boundary-layer thickness, and time by the associated diffusion scale. Every time-monotone solution in the Oleinik class extends globally in time. The Falkner--Skan boundary layer globally attracts every such unsteady semi-similar profile. The convergence rate is exponential for $m=1$ and algebraic for $m>1$. We also prove nonlinear stability of each admissible time-dependent semi-similar trajectory under small compatible perturbations that break the semi-similar ansatz. Together, these results provide a dynamical justification of the time-dependent semi-similar class within the full Prandtl theory. For semi-similar flows, the Crocco transformation reduces the problem to a one-dimensional degenerate parabolic equation. Combined with weighted barriers, comparison principles propagate time monotonicity and lead to global continuation. Zero-order convergence and a one-sided gradient estimate then produce uniform strict concavity after a transient period; this concavity supplies the damping needed for derivative decay. The same damping mechanism extends to the full ultraparabolic perturbation equation, allowing us to close the nonlinear stability estimates.

title: Robust Resource Allocation for STAR-RIS-Assisted ISAC Networks Using Deep Learning
authors: Yuwen Cao, Jiajun Wu, Howard H. Yang, Tomoaki Ohtsuki, Tony Q. S. Quek
abstract: In this paper, we focus on investigating the resource allocation in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system assisted by a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). Due to the coupled non-convex nature of the optimization problem, solving the above joint resource optimization problem while guaranteeing superior sensing performance is challenging, especially in dynamic environment. To conquer such challenge, prior iterative optimization algorithms have been presented. However, practical implementations of these prior algorithms face notable computational challenges, e.g., the reliance on accurate global channel information and the assumption of ideal phase shifts. In this context, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming and waveform in ISAC networks with low-overhead. In addition, we adopt the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) as the sensing performance metric, and the multi-user interference (MUI) energy as the communication performance metric for performance evaluation. Besides, our framework jointly optimizes the transmit beamforming, waveform and the STAR-RIS reflection/transmission coefficient matrices by minimizing the weighted sum of MUI energy and CRLB. Our study also considers the impact of imperfect channel information, making the research scenario more aligned with real-world applications. Simulation results validate that the proposed framework not only achieves higher sum-rate performance comparable to traditional iterative algorithms but also significantly reduces computational complexity in terms of algorithm execution time, as well as exhibits inherent robustness.

title: AirMPA: A Meteorology-to-Pollution Adapter for Global Air Quality Forecasting
authors: Yiheng Wang, Kai Zheng, Yuetan Lin, Fanglu Fan, Chenliang Tao, Guochao Chen, Hongliang Zhang, Hao Li
abstract: Accurate real-time forecasting of atmospheric pollutants is essential for reducing exposure risks and improving public health. Traditional numerical forecasting systems suffer from incomplete parameterizations, uncertain inputs, and high computational cost. Existing deep learning approaches improve efficiency, but often entangle meteorological and pollutant variables within unified forecasting frameworks, limiting flexibility and pollutant-specific representation learning. To address these challenges, we propose AirMPA, a decoupled autoregressive framework for meteorology-to-pollution forecasting. AirMPA predicts 13 atmospheric pollutants at 0.4° spatial resolution and 12-h temporal resolution using meteorological fields, emission priors, and historical pollutant concentrations. The model is built on an improved Swin-Transformer architecture with zonal release attention and dual-branch fusion, enabling more effective modeling of global transport continuity and heterogeneous pollutant dynamics. During training, AirMPA uses the fifth-generation atmospheric reanalysis from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ERA5) as meteorological forcing, while during inference it directly ingests forecast fields from external meteorological models, enabling stable autoregressive prediction up to 5 days ahead. Experiments show that AirMPA consistently outperforms Aurora and surpasses the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) in approximately 90% of pollutant-lead-time evaluation cases over the 5-day forecast horizon, while outperforming CAMS on all variables beyond 48 h. These results demonstrate the potential of decoupled meteorology-to-pollution forecasting for global air quality prediction.

title: Detection Augmented Learning In Non-Stationary Bandit Environments
authors: Argyrios Gerogiannis, Yu-Han Huang, Subhonmesh Bose, Venugopal V. Veeravalli
abstract: We study the problem of non-stationary bandits without knowledge of the environmental changes. We propose Detection Augmented Learning (DAL) a black-box paradigm that comprises three modular components: a bandit algorithm, a change detector, and a forced exploration schedule. This modular design enables its applicability across a broad spectrum of bandit problems, from classical to highly structured settings. First, we provide theoretical insights into DAL's strong empirical performance: a single regret bound shows that DAL transfers the regret of its stationary input to the piecewise stationary setting, attaining or improving the best known bounds in every setting considered. We further identify conditions under which DAL performs well in drifting environments. Then, we showcase DAL's practical performance and versatility through extensive experimentation in which DAL consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods, both prior-free and prior-based, across diverse non-stationary scenarios in nine bandit settings. Finally, we investigate the effectiveness of the forced exploration and show that a bandit-driven strategy improves performance and shortens detection delay.

title: See the Future, Classify the Present: Stochastic Latent World Modeling for Hyperspectral Images
authors: Muhammad Ahmad, Gemine Vivone, Ronny Hänsch, Ahmed Sohaib, Manuel Mazzara, Danfeng Hong
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) relies on static spatial-spectral representations learned from labeled samples, limiting its ability to model structured dependencies in the latent representation space. To address this limitation, this work proposes Stochastic Latent World Modeling (LWM), a trajectory-based representation-learning framework that enriches classification through stochastic latent-state prediction. Given a hyperspectral patch, LWM tokenizes and encodes spectral and spatial information separately using dedicated transformer branches, then fuses their outputs into a unified representation. This representation is further organized into an environment state that captures center, neighborhood, spectral, and global contextual information. A stochastic latent transition module then predicts multiple future latent states through Gaussian parameterization and reparameterization, with recurrent refinement used to model dependencies across successive states. The resulting latent trajectory is adaptively aggregated by a rollout planner to construct a planned representation, which is integrated with the base representation for final classification. By extending static spatial-spectral encoding with stochastic multi-step latent-state modeling, LWM enables the classifier to exploit structured dependencies in the representation space and provides richer features for HSIC. Across five benchmark datasets, LWM achieves overall accuracies ranging from 89.21% to 99.52%, demonstrating consistent classification performance under limited-label settings.

title: Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
authors: Yeoneung Kim, Donghyun Lee, Sung-Jun Son
abstract: We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $γ\geq -2$ and the uncut case $γ=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.

title: OpenSaC: A Python Library for Search as Code in Deep Research Agents
authors: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua, Ji-Rong Wen
abstract: Deep research agents investigate complex questions through iterative search, source examination, and evidence synthesis. A conventional workflow alternates reasoning with individual search and reading actions. Search as Code introduces a new paradigm: agents write programs that compose search, source reading, reranking, model calls, and local processing, returning selected observations for further reasoning. To support this workflow in existing coding agents, we present OpenSaC, an open-source Python library with a companion Search as Code skill. Configurable capability interfaces let agents combine these operations while retaining evidence for inspection and reuse. Compared with standard Codex using its built-in web search, the OpenSaC configuration uses less execution time and fewer model tokens on BrowseComp and WideSearch, with higher accuracy on BrowseComp and slightly lower row F1 on WideSearch. We aim to lower the barrier to adopting Search as Code and provide an open foundation for community development and transparent research on deep research agents.

title: What Is Under the Hood? A Cross-Ecosystem Study of Vulnerable Dependencies in Construction Software
authors: Mahzabin Tamanna, S M Jamil Uddin
abstract: The construction industry increasingly relies on software built from third-party components, yet the dependency composition and known-vulnerability exposure of construction-related software remain poorly analyzed. In this study, we conduct an empirical, cross-ecosystem investigation of 904 construction-related GitHub repositories spanning six construction functions and a multifunction category. Using commit-pinned repository snapshots and OSV-Scanner, we examine dependency assessability, known-vulnerability prevalence, severity, weakness classifications, and shared upstream exposure. Our results reveal that only 494 repositories (54.6%) completed vulnerability assessment, revealing substantial gaps in dependency visibility. Among successfully scanned repositories, 395 (80.0%) contained at least one dependency version associated with a published vulnerability advisory, and 97.2% of affected repositories contained a High or Critical severity risk. Additionally, Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) mapping identified recurring resource-consumption, path-traversal, information-exposure, and code-injection weaknesses. Vulnerability burden was uneven, with a median of 50 distinct advisory clusters per affected repository, while just two affected upstream package families collectively reached ~70% of affected repositories. These findings establish an empirical baseline for dependency assessability and known-vulnerability exposure in construction-related open-source software. Our findings underscore the importance of documenting assessment coverage, interpreting advisory matches in their deployment context, and examining shared upstream dependencies when evaluating construction software supply-chain security.

title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation
authors: Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Weishuo Sun, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu, Yuang Xie, Qicheng Zeng, Peng Ye, Jiajun Deng, Jianmin Ji
abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.

title: Cognitively Decoupled Meta-Induction for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Yuqian Wang, Yuanzheng Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Ke Xu, Bingxiang He, Jinghan Tan, Zijun Chen, Lu Chen, Yi-Xin Huo, Maosong Sun
abstract: In-context learning (ICL) tackles downstream tasks conditioned on demonstrations. This paradigm relies heavily on neighbor-based matching between queries and demonstrations, limiting out-of-distribution (OOD) performance. For better generalization, rule-based inductive reasoning derives task-level regularities, which we term task-level inductive representations (TIR), before directly answering. However, existing methods lack generalizable inductive ability across diverse tasks. Inspired by meta-learning, we propose Cognitive-Decoupling meta-Induction (CoDI) for TIR-based inductive reasoning on general tasks. CoDI comprises a Cognitive-Decoupling Framework for query-blind TIR induction, and a Dual-Loop Meta-Inductive Learning method for cross-task inducer optimization. Empirically, CoDI achieves substantial performance gains on five ID and OOD benchmarks, and preserves OOD gains without explicit induction at inference. Code is available at https://github.com/Yuqian-Wang2277/codi-meta-induction.

title: Compiling Environment Classifiers to Contextual Modal Types
authors: Tianyu Chen, Darshal Shetty, Jeremy G. Siek, Chao-Hong Chen, Weixi Ma, Arnaud Venet, Rocky Liu
abstract: Type systems for metaprogramming take one of two approaches to safeguarding the scopes of variables in generated code. They either use Environment Classifiers (EC) to identify scopes by name (Taha and Nielsen, 2003), or they use Contextual Modal Type Theory (CMTT) to match scopes by structure (Nanevski, Pfenning, and Pientka, 2008). In this paper, we connect these two approaches by compiling a calculus with polymorphic environment classifiers, subtyping, and mutable references to a CMTT-based calculus with polymorphic contexts, mutable references, and first-class substitutions. The key idea is to map each environment classifier to a context. We prove that the compilation preserves types and that compilation preserves the behavior of metaprograms. Both proofs are mechanized in Agda. The compilation shows that CMTT is at least as expressive as environment classifiers. We conjecture that the converse compilation is difficult, because environment classifiers impose a stricter regime on the metaprogram.

title: A Calibrated Instrument for Detecting Disposition Drift in Language Models
authors: Jerry Kaplan
